Rashi on Eruvin 75b:11:1.hebrew: הרי הוא כרבים - אם דר נכרי בפנימית ושני ישראלים בחיצונה, אוסרת דריסת רגלו עליהן עד שישכיר. ואליבא דשמואל אמרה ר"א למילתיה, דאי לרב אדא, מאי איריא נכרי? אפילו ישראל נמי אסר כי הוו שנים בחיצונה! והא ליכא למימר דביחיד בחיצונה אסר — דהשתא אפילו דר עמו בחצר עצמה, הא קי"ל כר"א בן יעקב, דאמר: עד שיהו שני ישראלים אוסרין זה על זה, דריסת רגלו לא כל שכן דלא אסרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:11:1.english: Behold, he is like many - If a gentile lives in the inner [courtyard] and two Jews [live] in the outer [courtyard], his right of passage prohibits them until he rents [out his rights]. And Rabbi Elazar stated his ruling in accordance with Shmuel; for if [it were] according to Rav Adda, why specifically a gentile? Even an [individual] Jew would also prohibit when there are two in the outer [courtyard]! And this cannot be said, that he prohibits [in the case of] an individual in the outer [courtyard] — for now, even if he lived with him in the courtyard itself, behold, we hold in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, who said: "[A gentile does not prohibit] unless there are two Jews who prohibit one another," [so in the case of] his right of passage, is it not all the more so that it does not prohibit?!

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:11:2.hebrew: דידע - שהוא שם יחידי, וידע שאין רגל המותרת אוסרת, ולא נפקא מינה חורבה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:11:2.english: [One] who knows - That he is there alone, and he knows that a permitted foot does not prohibit, and no mishap will result from it.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:12:1.hebrew: מפעא פעי - קלא אית ליה, והני לא איגור. ומאן דלא ידע שהוא דר שם יחידי, סבר דאין דריסת הרגל אוסרת, א"נ עירוב של פנימים וחיצונים מועיל במקום נכרי בלא שכירות:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:12:1.english: He would chatter - [Renting] generates publicity, and [everyone knows that] these [residents] did not rent [from him]. And one who does not know that he lives there alone would think that [having] right of way does not prohibit [carrying], or alternatively, [that] an eiruv of the inner and outer [residents] is effective in the presence of a gentile without renting.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:13:1.hebrew: י' בתים זה לפנים מזה - חיצון פתוח לחצר, וכולן דריסת רגלו עליו, ופנימי דורס על כולן, שאין לו יציאה אלא דרך זו. כולן נעשין בית שער לו, ואינן אוסרין על בני חצר אלא פנימי לבדו, כדאמרן בפירקין (דף עב:): "והדר שם אינו אוסר". הלכך, כשבאין שאר דיורין הפתוחין לחצר ולערב את חצירן — פנימי זה נותן פת, והשאר אין צריכין:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:13:1.english: Ten houses, one within the other - The outermost [house] opens into the courtyard, and all of them have right of passage through it, and the innermost [resident] treads through all of them, as he has no exit except via this route. All of them become a gatehouse for him, and they do not restrict the residents of the courtyard, but rather the innermost one alone [restricts them], as we said in our chapter (daf 72b): "And one who resides there does not restrict." Therefore, when the other residents whose [houses] open into the courtyard come to establish an eiruv for their courtyard, this innermost [resident] contributes bread, and the rest do not need to.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:14:1.english: Even the outer one - Must give the bread [for the eiruv].

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:14:2.english: The outer [house] of the innermost [one] - The ninth house [counting from] the courtyard:

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:16:1.hebrew: ג' בתים ביניהן - בית זה פתוח לחצר זו, וזה לזו, ובית אמצעי פתוח לב' הבתים:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:16:1.english: Three houses between them - This house opens to this courtyard, and that [house] to that [courtyard], and the middle house opens to the two houses.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:16:2.hebrew: זה בא בדרך זה - בן חצר זו בא דרך בית הפתוח לו, ונתן עירובו באמצעי, ועשה בית הפתוח לו כבית שער לעבור דרך עליו לאמצעי. וכן בן חצר האחרת עשה בית הפתוח לו כבית שער, ועירב באמצעי חצר האחרת. אין אחד מדיורי הבתים האלה צריך ליתן פת — אלו משום בית שער, ואמצעי משום בית שמניחין בו עירוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:16:2.english: This one comes through this [house] - A resident of this courtyard comes through the house that opens to him, and places his eiruv in the middle [house], and makes the house that opens to him like a gatehouse to pass through it to the middle [house]. And likewise, a resident of the other courtyard makes the house that opens to him like a gatehouse, and establishes the eiruv of the other courtyard in the middle [house]. None of the residents of these houses needs to contribute bread: these [outer ones] on account of [being a] gatehouse, and the middle [one] on account of [being the] house in which an eiruv is placed.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:1.hebrew: תניא נמי הכי - כרב יהודה, דהא "מקום אחד" דמתני' — בחיצונה קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:1.english: That was also taught [in a baraita like this] - In accordance with Rav Yehuda, for [when] the Mishnah states "one place," it means in the outer [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:2.english: Or of the inner, etc., they are both prohibited - As we explained.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:3.hebrew: נתנו את עירובן בפנימית ושכח אחד מן הפנימית שתיהן אסורות - דחיצונה מיתסרא בשכחה דפנימית, דלא מצי אסתלוקי מינה; ועוד, דליתיה לעירובה גבה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:3.english: [If] they placed their eiruv in the inner [courtyard] and one [resident] of the inner [courtyard] forgot, both of them are prohibited - For the outer [courtyard] is rendered prohibited by the forgetting [of a resident] of the inner [courtyard], as it cannot dissociate itself from it; and furthermore, because its eiruv is not with it.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:4.hebrew: שתיהן אסורות דברי ר"ע - ולא אמרי' תסתלק פנימית מינה, כדמפרש לקמיה, דעירוב החיצונה המונח לתוכה מרגילה שם:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:4.english: Both of them are prohibited, [this is] the statement of Rabbi Akiva - And we do not say [that] the inner [courtyard] may withdraw from it, as [the Gemara] explains below, that the eiruv of the outer [courtyard] placed inside it accustoms it [to enter] there.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:5.hebrew: בזו פנימית מותרת - דמשום שכחה דחיצונה לא מיתסרא, אלא אחדא דשא ומסתלקא מינה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:1:5.english: In this [case], the inner [courtyard] is permitted - For on account of the forgetting of [a resident of] the outer [courtyard], it is not prohibited; rather, it closes the door and withdraws from it:

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:4:1.hebrew: מבטלינן לך - וכי אמר ר"ע "פנימית אסורה", עד שתבטל לה חיצונה רשות הרגל עירובה קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:4:1.english: We renounce [our rights] to you - And when Rabbi Akiva said, “The inner [courtyard] is prohibited,” he meant [prohibited only] until the outer [courtyard] renounces to it the right of access [conferred by] its eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:4:2.hebrew: אין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר - ואי אמרת תיסר עלה, מעוותא לה. הלכך, אמרה לה: לתקוני שיתפתיך ולא לעוותי:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:4:2.english: There is no renunciation of rights from courtyard to courtyard - And if you were to say that [the inner courtyard] should be prohibited on its account, [that would be] causing it detriment. Therefore, [the inner courtyard] says to it: “I joined with you to [my] benefit and not to [my] detriment.”

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:5:1.english: Shmuel and Rabbi Yoḥanan - Who disagreed earlier in our chapter (Eruvin 68a) regarding renunciation [of rights] from [one] courtyard to [another] courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:6:1.hebrew: דאסרן אהדדי - ע"י הרגל העירוב, ומתוך שאוסרין — מבטלין. וכי אמרי אנא — בשתי חצירות ופתח ביניהן ולא עירבו, והוצרכה זו לטלטל לרשות של זו — אין מבטלין:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:6:1.english: Which render each other prohibited - Through the customary practice of the eruv; and since they render [each other] prohibited, they may renounce [their rights]. And when I [Shmuel] said [that there is no renunciation of rights from courtyard to courtyard, I said it] regarding two courtyards with a doorway between them that did not make an eruv [together], and this [courtyard] needed to carry into the domain of that [courtyard — in such a case,] they do not renounce [their rights].

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:7:1.hebrew: אפילו לרבנן - דרבנן נמי מודו דיש ביטול, ואפילו הכי עיוות קרי ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:7:1.english: Even in accordance with the Rabbis - For the Rabbis also agree that there is renunciation of rights, and even so he called it a distortion:

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:7:2.english: That it says to it - The inner [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:7:3.hebrew: אדמבטלית לי - בעוד שלא בטלתה, את אוסרת עלי. הלכך: דל אנת ודל ביטולך, דלא בעינא ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:7:3.english: Until you renounce [rights] in my favor - As long as you have not renounced [your rights], you restrict me. Therefore: Take away yourself and take away your renunciation, for I do not want it.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:7:4.hebrew: מי קאסרת - חצר על חברתה בפתח שביניהן בלא עירוב, דאי אמרת תבטיל, ניהוי עיוות:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:7:4.english: Does it prohibit - [Does] one courtyard [prohibit] the other through the doorway between them without an eiruv, such that if you were to say it should renounce [its rights], it would be a detriment?

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:8:1.hebrew: אמר רב יוסף תני רבי אם היו ג' - בין ב' החצירות, אוסרין. ולא מיבעיא שנים בפנימית, דהויא רגל האסורה; אלא אפי' שנים בחיצונה — אסור, עד שעירבו שתיהן יחד, גזירה משום רבים בפנימית:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:8:1.english: Rav Yosef said, Rabbi teaches: If there were three - [Divided] between the two courtyards, they prohibit [each other]. And it is not necessary [to state this when there are] two in the inner [courtyard], for it is a prohibited foot; rather, even [when there are] two in the outer [courtyard], it is prohibited until both of them make an eiruv together, [as] a decree on account of [having] many in the inner [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:9:1.hebrew: לא תציתו ליה - למאי דתני לה משמיה דרבי, דלאו מתני' היא, אלא שמעתא (דרב יוסף) היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:9:1.english: Do not listen to him - [Do not listen] to that which he teaches in the name of Rabbi, for it is not a Mishnah, but rather an Amoraic teaching (of Rav Yosef).

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:9:2.hebrew: ואנא אמריתה ניהלה משמיה דרב אדא - ומן הטעם הזה אמרתי לו: הואיל ואני קורא רבים בחיצונה, גזרי' משום רבים בפנימית. רב יוסף חלה ושכח תלמודו:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:9:2.english: And I told it to him in the name of Rav Adda - And for this reason I said to him: Since I call them “many” in the outer [courtyard], we decree on account of [a case of] many in the inner [courtyard]. Rav Yosef had fallen ill and forgotten his learning.

Rashi on Eruvin 75b:9:3.hebrew: רבים ברבי אחלף לי - הטעם שאמר לי ״רבים בחיצונה״ נתחלף לי ב״רבי״. כששכחתי הדבר בחליי וחזרתי לגירסתי הראשונה, נזכרתי שהוזכר לי ״רבים״ בדבר, וסבור הייתי שנאמר לי בשם רבי:
Rashi on Eruvin 75b:9:3.english: "Many" was confused for me with "Rabbi" - The reason that he told me, "many in the outer [courtyard]," became confused for me with "Rabbi." When I forgot the matter during my illness and returned to my original learning, I remembered that "many" had been mentioned to me regarding the matter, and I thought that it had been said to me in the name of Rabbi.

Tosafot on Eruvin 75b:11:1.hebrew: נכרי הרי הוא כרבים - אליבא דשמואל קאמר, כדפי' בקונט', דליכא למימר דביחיד בחיצונה נמי אסר — דאפי' היה דר עמו בחצר לא אסר, דקיימא לן כראב"י, כ"ש דריסת רגל דלא אסרה. וכן מוכחא בהדיא לעיל גבי ישראל ונכרי בפנימית וישראל בחיצונה: דאי ליכא ישראל בפנימית אלא נכרי לחודיה — לא אסר. וא"ת: ולמה ליה למימר "הרי הוא כרבים"? אפילו לא הוו כרבים אסר, דכיון דיש שני ישראלים בחיצונה ואוסרין זה על זה, ויש לו דריסת רגל עליהן! וי"ל: כיון דישראל לא אסר, נכרי נמי לא אסר — דאין להחמיר בנכרי יותר מבישראל אי לאו דהוו כרבים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 75b:11:1.english: "A gentile is considered like many" - [Rabbi Elazar] is speaking in accordance with [the view of] Shmuel, as was explained in the Kunteres [by Rashi]. For it cannot be said that [he meant that a gentile] prohibits even when there is [only] an individual in the outer [courtyard] — since even if [the gentile] had been living with him [directly] in the courtyard, he would not prohibit [him], as we maintain in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov; all the more so [with regard to] right of passage, that it does not prohibit. And so it is proven explicitly above regarding an Israelite and a gentile in the inner [courtyard] and an Israelite in the outer [courtyard]: that if there is no Israelite in the inner [courtyard], but rather a gentile alone, he does not prohibit. And if you say: But why did he need to say [that the gentile] "is considered like many"? Even if they were not [treated as] many, he should prohibit, since there are two Israelites in the outer [courtyard] who prohibit one another, and [the gentile] has a right of passage over them! And one can say: Since an [individual] Israelite does not prohibit, a gentile also would not prohibit, for one should not be more stringent with a gentile than with an Israelite, were it not that he is [considered] like many.

Tosafot on Eruvin 75b:15:1.hebrew: ורבי יוחנן סבר בית שער דיחיד לא הוי בית שער - והא דאמר בפ' כיצד משתתפין (לקמן עירובין דף פה:): "כל מקום שאמרו חכמים: 'הדר שם אינו אוסר' — הנותן שם עירובו אינו עירוב, חוץ מבית שער דיחיד", פי': דאף על גב דהדר שם אינו אוסר, הנותן שם עירובו הוי עירוב — אתי נמי כר' יוחנן; דהתם איירי בבית שער דחצר, כדפי' שם בקונטרס, דאינו עשוי לדירה; אבל הכא, העשוי לדירה — אוסר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 75b:15:1.english: "And Rabbi Yoḥanan holds [that] the gatehouse of an individual is not a gatehouse" - And that which [the Gemara] said in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Mishtatfin (below, Eruvin 85b): "Any place with regard to which the Sages said: 'One who resides there does not render [it] forbidden,' one who places his eiruv there, [his] is not an eiruv, except for the gatehouse of an individual" — meaning, that even though one who resides there does not render [it] forbidden, one who places his eiruv there, [it] is a [valid] eiruv — [this] also accords with Rabbi Yoḥanan; for there it is dealing with the gatehouse of a courtyard, as [Rashi] explained there in the Kunteres, which is not made for dwelling; but here, [a house] that is made for dwelling renders [it] forbidden.

Tosafot on Eruvin 75b:6:1.hebrew: עד כאן לא קאמר ר"ע הכא אלא בב' חצירות זו לפנים מזו דאסרן אהדדי - יש לישב הך סוגיא נמי אליבא דרבא, דאמר לעיל (עירובין דף סו.) לשמואל דבשתי חצירות זו לפנים מזו פעמים אין מבטלין, אע"ג דאסרן אהדדי — דהכא קאמר: דאסרן אהדדי בפשיעות בני חיצונה, שהורגלו עירובן בפנימית, דשכח א' מהן ולא עירב. אבל בכל הנהו דאמר שמואל אין מבטלין, מי אסרן אהדדי בפשיעה? דכי נתנו עירובן בחיצונה ושכח אחד מהן ולא עירב, אין האיסור בא ע"י שפשעו במה שהרגילו עירובן ושכח אחד מהם ולא עירב, דבלאו הכי היה להם דריסת הרגל. ואין לתמוה: היאך מתוקם לרבא שמואל כר"ע וכרבנן, הא ע"כ כר"ע דוקא ס"ל, כדפי' בקונטרס לעיל? דמ"מ בעיקר פלוגתייהו, דאין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר, מוקמי נפשיה בכולהו. וא"ת: ולאביי, דאמר שתי חצירות זו לפנים מזו דמבטלין בכל ענין לשמואל, (מי נימא) שמואל כר"ע ולא כרבנן, דלרבנן ב' חצירות זו לפנים מזו אין מבטלין? וי"ל: דהוה מפרש כר' יוחנן דבסמוך: "עד כאן לא קאמרי רבנן התם אלא דאמר' לה: אדמבטלת לי קאסרת עלי בפשיעותא שהרגלת עירובך ושכח אחד מכם":
Tosafot on Eruvin 75b:6:1.english: Rabbi Akiva stated [his opinion] only here, with regard to two courtyards, one within the other, which render each other prohibited — This sugya can also be reconciled according to [the view of] Rava, who said above (Eruvin 66a) according to Shmuel that in [the case of] two courtyards, one within the other, sometimes they do not renounce [their rights], even though they render each other prohibited. For here [the Gemara] means that they render each other prohibited through the negligence of the residents of the outer [courtyard], who were accustomed to place their eiruv in the inner [courtyard], when one of them forgot and did not establish an eiruv. However, in all those [other cases] where Shmuel said they do not renounce [their rights], do they render each other prohibited through negligence? For when they placed their eiruv in the outer [courtyard] and one of them forgot and did not establish an eiruv, the prohibition does not come about through their having been negligent in making their eiruv habitual and one of them having forgotten and not established an eiruv, since even without this [the residents of the inner courtyard] had the right of passage [through the outer courtyard]. And one should not wonder: How can Shmuel be established according to Rava [both] in accordance with Rabbi Akiva and in accordance with the Rabbis, when perforce he holds specifically in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, as Rashi explained above? For nevertheless, in their fundamental dispute — that there is no renunciation of rights from courtyard to courtyard — [Shmuel] aligns himself with both of them. And if you say: But according to Abaye, who said that in [the case of] two courtyards, one within the other, they renounce [their rights] in all circumstances according to Shmuel, (shall we say that) Shmuel [rules] in accordance with Rabbi Akiva and not in accordance with the Rabbis, for according to the Rabbis, [in the case of] two courtyards, one within the other, they do not renounce [their rights]? And one can say: He would explain [the position of the Rabbis] like Rabbi Yoḥanan just adjacent [in the next segment]: "The Rabbis stated [their opinion] there only because [the inner courtyard] said to [the outer courtyard]: Until you renounce [your rights] in my favor, you prohibit [carrying] upon me through negligence, for you made your eiruv habitual and one of you forgot."

Tosafot on Eruvin 75b:9:1.hebrew: ואני קורא בהם רבים בחיצונה - ויסברו שיש כמו כן שנים בפנימית, ולא עירבו. אבל כשיש שנים בפנימית ועירבו — לא גזרינן אטו לא עירבו, דעירבו אטו לא עירבו לא גזרינן. אבל כשיש אחד בפנימית ולא עירבו — יסברו שהם שנים כמו בחיצונה, והרי לא עירבו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 75b:9:1.english: "Since I call them many in the outer [courtyard]" - And [people] will think that there are likewise two [residents] in the inner [courtyard], and they did not make an eiruv. But when there are two in the inner [courtyard] and they made an eiruv, we do not decree on account of [a case where] they did not make an eiruv, for we do not decree [concerning a case where] they made an eiruv on account of [a case where] they did not make an eiruv. However, when there is one [resident] in the inner [courtyard] and they did not make an eiruv, [people] will think that they are two, just like in the outer [courtyard], and behold, they did not make an eiruv.
